description: Cache entire CD images in memory.
help:
Reads the entire CD image(s) into memory at startup(which will cause a small delay).  Can help obviate emulation hiccups due to emulated CD access.  May cause more harm than good on low memory systems, systems with swap enabled, and/or when the disc images in question are on a fast SSD.

help:
Higher values correspond to better SNR and better preservation of higher frequencies("brightness"), at the cost of increased computational complexity and a negligible increase in latency.

Higher values will also slightly increase the probability of sample clipping(relevant if Mednafen's volume control settings are set too high), due to increased (time-domain) ringing.
Lower values correspond to better matching of the output rate of the resampler to the actual desired output rate, at the expense of increased RAM usage and poorer CPU cache utilization.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

Opacity is specified in %; IE a value of "100" will give entirely black scanlines.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

Obviously, this will only work with the OpenGL "video.driver" setting, and only on cards and OpenGL implementations that support shaders, otherwise you will get a black screen, or Mednafen may display an error message when starting up. When a shader is enabled, the "<system>.videoip" setting is ignored.

Higher values correspond to better SNR and better preservation of higher frequencies("brightness"), at the cost of increased computational complexity and a negligible(<0.5ms) increase in latency.

The destination rectangle is NOT altered by this setting, so if you have xscale and yscale set to "2", and try to use a 3x scaling filter like hq3x, the image is not going to look that great. description: Enable bilinear interpolation on the chroma channel of RAINBOW YUV output.
help: This is an enhancement-related setting.  Enabling it may cause graphical glitches with some games.
Higher values correspond to better SNR and better preservation of higher frequencies("brightness"), at the cost of increased computational complexity and a negligible increase in latency.
Lower values correspond to better matching of the output rate of the resampler to the actual desired output rate, at the expense of increased RAM usage and poorer CPU cache utilization.

Opacity is specified in %; IE a value of "100" will give entirely black scanlines.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

Obviously, this will only work with the OpenGL "video.driver" setting, and only on cards and OpenGL implementations that support shaders, otherwise you will get a black screen, or Mednafen may display an error message when starting up. When a shader is enabled, the "<system>.videoip" setting is ignored.

Enable BIOS ROM image sanity checks.
help: Enables blacklisting of known bad BIOS dumps and known BIOS versions that don't match the region of the hardware being emulated.

Sanity checks are only performed on discs detected(via heuristics) to be PS1 discs.  The checks primarily consist of ensuring that Q subchannel data is as expected for a typical commercially-released PS1 disc.

Disabling aspect ratio correction with this setting should be considered a hack.

If disabling it to allow for sharper pixels by also separately disabling interpolation(though using Mednafen's "autoipsharper" OpenGL shader is usually a better option), remember to use scale factors that are multiples of 2, or else games that use high-resolution and interlaced modes will have distorted pixels.

Disabling aspect ratio correction with this setting will allow for the QuickTime movie recording feature to produce much smaller files using much less CPU time.

Rumble is emulated, but currently only supported on Linux, and MS Windows via the XInput API and XInput-compatible gamepads/joysticks. Opacity is specified in %; IE a value of "100" will give entirely black scanlines.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

Obviously, this will only work with the OpenGL "video.driver" setting, and only on cards and OpenGL implementations that support shaders, otherwise you will get a black screen, or Mednafen may display an error message when starting up. When a shader is enabled, the "<system>.videoip" setting is ignored.

Higher values correspond to better SNR and better preservation of higher frequencies("brightness"), at the cost of increased computational complexity and a negligible increase in latency.

Higher values will also slightly increase the probability of sample clipping(relevant if Mednafen's volume control settings are set too high), due to increased (time-domain) ringing.

help:
Higher values correspond to better SNR and better preservation of higher frequencies("brightness"), at the cost of increased computational complexity and a negligible increase in latency.

Higher values will also slightly increase the probability of sample clipping(relevant if Mednafen's volume control settings are set too high), due to increased (time-domain) ringing.
Lower values correspond to better matching of the output rate of the resampler to the actual desired output rate, at the expense of increased RAM usage and poorer CPU cache utilization.

Opacity is specified in %; IE a value of "100" will give entirely black scanlines.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

Obviously, this will only work with the OpenGL "video.driver" setting, and only on cards and OpenGL implementations that support shaders, otherwise you will get a black screen, or Mednafen may display an error message when starting up. When a shader is enabled, the "<system>.videoip" setting is ignored.

options.label: Auto Interpolation
options.description: Will automatically interpolate on each axis if the corresponding effective scaling factor is not an integer.

options.label: Sharper Auto Interpolation
options.description: Same as "autoip", but when interpolation is done, it is done in a manner that will reduce blurriness if possible.

When enabled, it may be prudent to disable the scanlines effect controlled by the "<system>.shader.goat.slen" setting, or else the scanline effect may look objectionable.

help: The destination rectangle is NOT altered by this setting, so if you have xscale and yscale set to "2", and try to use a 3x scaling filter like hq3x, the image is not going to look that great. The nearest-neighbor scalers are intended for use with bilinear interpolation enabled, for a sharper image, though the "autoipsharper" shader may provide better results.

description: Enable 1-frame speculative execution for video output.

When using ALSA sound output under Linux, the "sound.device" setting "default" is Mednafen's default, IE "hw:0", not ALSA's "default". If you want to use ALSA's "default", use "sexyal-literal-default".
The following choices are possible, sorted by preference, high to low, when "default" driver is used, but dependent on being compiled in.

options.label: Default
options.description: Selects the default sound driver.

options.label: ALSA
options.description: The default for Linux(if available).

options.label: OpenBSD Audio
options.description: The default for OpenBSD.

options.label: Open Sound System
options.description:
The default for non-Linux UN*X/POSIX/BSD(other than OpenBSD) systems, or anywhere ALSA is unavailable. If the ALSA driver gives you problems, you can try using this one instead.

If you are using OSSv4 or newer, you should edit "/usr/lib/oss/conf/osscore.conf", uncomment the max_intrate= line, and change the value from 100(default) to 1000(or higher if you know what you're doing), and restart OSS. Otherwise, performance will be poor, and the sound buffer size in Mednafen will be orders of magnitude larger than specified.

If the sound buffer size is still excessively larger than what is specified via the "sound.buffer_time" setting, you can try setting "sound.period_time" to 2666, and as a last resort, 5333, to work around a design flaw/limitation/choice in the OSS API and OSS implementation.

options.label: WASAPI(Shared Mode)
options.description: The default when it's available(running on Microsoft Windows Vista and newer).

options.label: DirectSound
options.description: The default for Microsoft Windows XP and older.

options.label: WASAPI(Exclusive Mode)
options.description: Experimental exclusive-mode WASAPI driver, usable on Windows Vista and newer.  Use it for lower-latency sound.  May not work properly on all sound cards.

options.label: Simple Directmedia Layer
options.description: This driver is not recommended, but it serves as a backup driver if the others aren't available. Its performance is generally sub-par, requiring higher latency or faster CPUs/SMP for glitch-free playback, except where the OS provides a sound callback API itself, such as with Mac OS X and BeOS.

options.label: JACK
options.description: The latency reported during startup is for the local sound buffer only and does not include server-side latency.  Please note that video card drivers(in the kernel or X), and hardware-accelerated OpenGL, may interfere with jackd's ability to effectively run with realtime response.

help:
Currently only affects OSS, ALSA, WASAPI(exclusive mode), and SDL output.  A value of 0 defers to the default in the driver code in SexyAL.

Note: This is not the "sound buffer size" setting, that would be "sound.buffer_time".

help:
Disabling aspect ratio correction with this setting should be considered a hack.

If disabling it to allow for sharper pixels by also separately disabling interpolation(though using Mednafen's "autoipsharper" OpenGL shader is usually a better option), remember to use scale factors that are multiples of 2, or else games that use high-resolution and interlaced modes will have distorted pixels.

Disabling aspect ratio correction with this setting will allow for the QuickTime movie recording feature to produce much smaller files using much less CPU time.

options.label: Standard Output
options.description: Intended for debug text; escape characters(0x1B) will be filtered from the output.

description: Attempt to auto-detect region of game.

help: Used if region autodetection fails or is disabled.

Opacity is specified in %; IE a value of "100" will give entirely black scanlines.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

0 is lowest quality and CPU usage, 10 is highest quality and CPU usage.  The resampler that this setting refers to is used for converting from 44.1KHz to the sampling rate of the host audio device Mednafen is using.  Changing Mednafen's output rate, via the "sound.rate" setting, to "44100" may bypass the resampler, which can decrease CPU usage by Mednafen, and can increase or decrease audio quality, depending on various operating system and hardware factors.

Obviously, this will only work with the OpenGL "video.driver" setting, and only on cards and OpenGL implementations that support shaders, otherwise you will get a black screen, or Mednafen may display an error message when starting up. When a shader is enabled, the "<system>.videoip" setting is ignored.

options.label: Auto Interpolation
options.description: Will automatically interpolate on each axis if the corresponding effective scaling factor is not an integer.

options.label: Sharper Auto Interpolation
options.description: Same as "autoip", but when interpolation is done, it is done in a manner that will reduce blurriness if possible.

options.label: SABR v3.0

description: Force interlaced video to be treated as progressive.

When enabled, it may be prudent to disable the scanlines effect controlled by the "<system>.shader.goat.slen" setting, or else the scanline effect may look objectionable.

The destination rectangle is NOT altered by this setting, so if you have xscale and yscale set to "2", and try to use a 3x scaling filter like hq3x, the image is not going to look that great. The nearest-neighbor scalers are intended for use with bilinear interpolation enabled, for a sharper image, though the "autoipsharper" shader may provide better results.

help: This setting refers to pixels before vb.xscale(fs) scaling is taken into consideration.  For example, a value of "100" here will result in a separation of 300 screen pixels if vb.xscale(fs) is set to "3".

The destination rectangle is NOT altered by this setting, so if you have xscale and yscale set to "2", and try to use a 3x scaling filter like hq3x, the image is not going to look that great. The nearest-neighbor scalers are intended for use with bilinear interpolation enabled, for a sharper image, though the "autoipsharper" shader may provide better results.

description: Enable time synchronization(waiting) for frame blitting.
help:
Disable to reduce latency, at the cost of potentially increased video "juddering", with the maximum reduction in latency being about 1 video frame's time.
Will work best with emulated systems that are not very computationally expensive to emulate, combined with running on a relatively fast CPU.

The cursor will still be forcibly hidden in relative mouse mode(used automatically when emulating a mouse input device in fullscreen mode or in windowed mode and input grabbing is toggled on), and forcibly shown in the debugger.

description: Deinterlacer to use for interlaced video.

Like the "blend" deinterlacer, but the blending is done in a manner that respects gamma, reducing unwanted brightness changes, at the cost of increased CPU usage.

options.label: OpenGL
options.description: All video-related Mednafen features are available with this video driver.

options.label: Software Blitting to Framebuffer
options.description: Slower with lower-quality scaling than OpenGL, but if you don't have hardware-accelerated OpenGL rendering, it will probably be faster than software OpenGL rendering. Bilinear interpolation not available. OpenGL shaders do not work with this output method, of course.

help: Enabling may result in a noticeable negative impact on performance with the "softfb" video driver, and with the "opengl" video driver on underpowered GPUs.
Disable for rendering code performance testing.

description: Display to use with fullscreen mode.
help: Specify -1 to use the display on which the center of the window lies in windowed mode.

description: Preferred source data pixel format for emulated video.
help: Using hicolor(RGB555/RGB565) formats may boost performance, but at the cost of color fidelity.  Noticeability of color degradation depends on the emulated system and features, such as custom palettes or NTSC blitter, being used.  When hicolor format support is not available for the emulation module or special scaler being used, Mednafen will automatically fall back to using a truecolor format.  Examine Mednafen's startup output to see the actual OpenGL texture formats being used.

help: The only game this setting is known to affect is "Digimon Tamers - Battle Spirit".

Opacity is specified in %; IE a value of "100" will give entirely black scanlines.

Negative values are the same as positive values for non-interlaced video, but for interlaced video will cause the scanlines to be overlaid over the previous(if the "video.deinterlacer" setting is set to "weave", the default) field's lines.

Obviously, this will only work with the OpenGL "video.driver" setting, and only on cards and OpenGL implementations that support shaders, otherwise you will get a black screen, or Mednafen may display an error message when starting up. When a shader is enabled, the "<system>.videoip" setting is ignored.
